item.title: Direct Organozirconium‐Catalyzed Copolymerization of Propylene with Phosphino‐Olefins: Access to Isotactic Phosphine‐Functionalized Polypropylenes for Diverse Functions
item.description:
We report the synthesis of phosphine-functionalized isotactic polypropylenes (PFiPPs) via direct copolymerization of propylene + phosphino-olefin comonomers using a rac-[Me2Si(indenyl)2]ZrMe2 catalyst. The process shows high activity (2940 kg mol− 1 h− 1 atm− 1), M ns, and isotacticity (96% mmmm). PFiPPs are effective Suzuki-Miyaura coupling catalyst supports with negligible leaching, and provide enhanced interfacial shear adhesion.


ABSTRACT

Efficient development of functionalized polypropylenes is of fundamental scientific and technological interest but has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the efficient synthesis of a phosphine-functionalized isotactic polypropylene (PFiPP) series via direct propylene – phosphino-alkene copolymerization, mediated by the activated ansa-bis(indenyl)zirconium catalyst, rac-Me2Si(indenyl)2ZrR+/B(C6F5)4 −. The copolymerizations are highly efficient and selective, with 25°C turnover frequencies up to 2940 kg/(mol·h·atm) with 2.0 mol% phosphine incorporation, and high product isotacticity (96% mmmm). The high stereoregularity reflects experimentally- and DFT-identified steric and electronic effects imposed by the C2 -symmetric catalyst which mediates enantioselective olefin insertion into the Zr–C bond to promote stereoregular chain propagation. These phosphine-functionalized isotactic polypropylenes serve as effective PdCl2 ligands for high-activity Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling catalysis with negligible metal leaching. Regarding interfacial properties, aluminum adhesion measurements reveal that phosphine incorporation significantly enhances PFiPP shear strength versus that of pristine isotactic iPP by six-fold.

item.title: Hierarchically Porous Unsubstituted Olefin‐Linked COF With Synergistically Enhanced Electronic and Ionic Conductivities for High‐Performance Lithium‐Ion Battery Cathodes
item.description:
An unsubstituted olefin–linked, highly crystalline COF material with dual redox centers enables synergistic ion/electron transport, high capacity, and ultralong-life cathodic lithium-ion storage.


ABSTRACT

The development of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with synergistically enhanced ionic/electronic conductivities, improved active site utilization, and increased chemical stability for achieving high-performance lithium–ion battery (LIB) cathodes remain a significant challenge. Here, we report the rational design of a novel unsubstituted olefin–linked, highly crystalline COF (namely HATN–ICTO COF) as a cathode for LIBs. The HATN–ICTO COF integrates extended fully conjugated π–networks, hierarchical porosity, and dual redox–active centers, enabling a synergistic improvement in ionic and electronic conductivity as well as a high theoretical capacity. This unique unsubstituted olefin linkage also endows the COF with excellent chemical stability, thereby ensuring long-term cycling performance. Meanwhile, the hierarchical porous architecture of the COF can effectively buffer the volume expansion during repeated charge–discharge processes, mitigating electrode damage. The COF delivers a high specific capacity of 293 mAh g− 1 at 0.1 A g− 1 and maintains 206 mAh g− 1 at 10.0 A g− 1, with outstanding cycling performance of 155 mAh g− 1 at 5.0 A g− 1 after 18,000 cycles. Additionally, a pouch cell based on the HATN–ICTO COF//Li configuration was also demonstrated. This work provides fundamental insights into structure–property relationships governing charge delocalization and redox activity in COFs.

item.title: Oxygen Facilitated Aqueous Photomediated‐RAFT Polymerization: Just Add Salt
item.description:
Adding basic salt to PET-RAFT polymerization significantly increases the oxygen tolerance of the system by incorporating oxygen into the reaction. This method still maintained a high deal of control and livingness over the polymer. This approach was able to be expanded to work using natural sunlight and a commercially available Vitamin B2 tablet. These photopolymerizations were found to only proceed to high conversion in the presence of both oxygen and salt.


ABSTRACT

In this work, we report the first example of a novel oxygen-facilitated photoinitiation system by employing a combination of riboflavin 5’-monophosphate sodium salt (Vitamin B2) and disodium hydrogen phosphate (Na2HPO4) for conducting reversible addition–fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) polymerization. Under blue LED irradiation (λ = 451 nm) and an oxygen atmosphere, the bioactive form of riboflavin, flavin mononucleotide, in the presence of first Na2HPO4 and then extended to other salts, was able to initiate the controlled RAFT polymerization of N,N-dimethylacrylamide. The resulting polymer was found to also possess excellent chain fidelity after chain extension via characterization by gel permeation chromatography. These photopolymerizations were found to only proceed to high conversion in the presence of both oxygen and salt. Exploiting the oxygen-facilitated and aqueous nature of our system, we could achieve microliter-scale polymerization in mammalian cell culture medium in the presence of live cells.

item.title: An Adsorption‐Driven Solvophobic Interface for Stable Lithium‐Rich Manganese‐Based Lithium Metal Batteries
item.description:
Perfluorobutanesulfonyl fluoride (NfF) preferentially anchors to lithium-rich manganese-based cathodes, creating a solvophobic interphase that excludes carbonate solvents. This molecular barrier suppresses electrolyte oxidation and transition-metal (TM) dissolution while facilitating lithium-ion transport. The resulting interface supports over 1000 cycles at 3 C and 88% capacity retention after 50 cycles in 1.2 Ah lithium-metal pouch cells at 4.8 V.


ABSTRACT

Lithium-rich manganese-based (LRMO) oxides represent the premier cathode candidates for next-generation high-energy-density batteries due to high specific capacity exceeding 300 mAh g−1. However, the practical deployment of LRMO cathodes under high voltages (>4.8 V) is severely hindered by severe electrolyte oxidation and transition-metal (TM) dissolution. Herein, perfluorobutanesulfonyl fluoride (NfF) is introduced as a multifunctional additive to construct a robust solvophobic interphase on LRMO cathodes. The -SO2F group preferentially anchors to exposed TM sites, suppressing metal dissolution, while the perfluorinated chain excludes free solvent molecules from the cathode surface and mitigates oxidative electrolyte decomposition. The resulting inorganic-rich (LiF/Li x SO y ) engineered interface mitigates the irreversible layered-to-spinel phase transition and inhibits TM crosstalk to the lithium metal anode, ensuring exceptional structural integrity and rapid ionic transport kinetics. Consequently, Li||LRMO coin cells sustain over 1000 cycles at 3 C. The Li||LRMO full cells based on a 40 µm lithium anode and cathode loading of 8 mg cm−2 retain 173 mAh g−1 after 110 cycles. Moreover, the 1.2 Ah Li||LRMO pouch cells achieve 88% capacity retention after 50 cycles at 4.8 V. This work demonstrates solvophobic interphase engineering as an effective strategy for stabilizing high-voltage cathodes through coordinated regulation of interfacial chemistry and electrolyte accessibility.

item.title: Solvent‐Induced Reversible Phase Transition in Microporous Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks for Molecular‐Sieving Separation of CO2 and C2H2
item.description:
We report the construction of a microporous hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF) which undergoes a reversible structural transformation upon solvent removal. It demonstrates pore geometry that closely match the molecular size of CO2 while fully excluding C2H2. The size-sieving behavior yields high-purity C2H2 and the adsorbent can be regenerated simply by gas purging at ambient conditions.


ABSTRACT

Efficient separation of carbon dioxide (CO2) from acetylene (C2H2) remains a critical challenge in the chemical industry for C2H2 purification, due to their highly similar molecular sizes and physicochemical property. Here we report a HOF material, denoted HIAM-105, assembled from a tetracarboxylic acid building block. It undergoes reversible structural transformation upon solvent removal and inclusion. The guest-free structure (HIAM-105a) features precisely matched pore dimensions with CO2 molecules while fully excluding C2H2, enabling molecular sieving separation of CO2/C2H2. At 298 K and 1 bar, HIAM-105a achieves a CO2 adsorption capacity of 44.0 cm3 g−1, resulting in a CO2/C2H2 adsorption capacity ratio as high as 23.9, which outperforms most previously reported sieving adsorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm that HIAM-105a can produce C2H2 with ultrahigh purity from CO2/C2H2 mixtures, and more importantly, it can be readily regenerated through gas purging at ambient conditions.

item.title: Fully π‐Conjugated Nonvolatile n‐Type Additives Toward 21% Efficiency in Organic Solar Cells
item.description:
A conjugated electrostatic coupling modulation strategy induces ordered fibrillar crystallization, promoting charge transport and suppressing recombination to achieve an OSC efficiency of 21%.


ABSTRACT

Solid additive engineering represents a key strategy to modulate the morphology of organic solar cells via intermolecular interactions (van der Waals forces, hydrogen bonds, and dipole interaction) with photoactive materials. However, these weak interactions lack sufficient capacity to control the crystallization and phase separation of active layer. Here, we developed a conjugated electrostatic coupling strategy to strengthen the intermolecular forces between solid additives and donor/acceptor. The solid additive we designed possesses a fully conjugated structure that can generate strong electrostatic potential interaction, therefore a small amount of solid additive (3 wt%) facilitate ordered crystalline fibril growth of polymer donor and dense molecular packing of acceptor. In addition, the n-type nature and nonvolatile feature of solid additive promotes the electron transport capacity and stability of the active layer. As a result, the optimal device achieved a state-of-the-art efficiency of 21.02% (certificated to 20.55%), due to the prolonged exciton lifetime, suppressed charge recombination, and enhanced charge collection efficiency. This work establishes a new paradigm for solid additive engineering in organic photovoltaics.

item.title: Anion‐Site Coupling Programs Interfacial Hydration for Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation
item.description:
Coupled copper and bicarbonate sites establish a locally anchored hydration network that sustains interfacial water and hydrogen bond connectivity against the cathodic double layer, thereby lowering proton transfer barriers and enabling diverse electrocatalytic hydrogenation pathways.


ABSTRACT

Electrolyte anions are generally considered passive spectators at cathodically polarized interfaces, where electrostatic exclusion and strong solvation limit their access to catalytic sites. Here we establish anion-site coupling as a strategy to program interfacial hydration and accelerate near-neutral electrocatalytic hydrogenation. Molecularly defined Cu2+ sites coordinated by hexahydroxytriphenylene on oxidized carbon black provide accessible coordination motifs that selectively couple with oxygen-containing anions. Among HCO3 −, CO3 2−, and SO4 2−, bicarbonate forms Cu2+─HCO3 − coupled sites that locally anchor water at the catalyst interface, replenishing otherwise depleted hydration regions and restoring hydrogen-bond connectivity for proton transfer. This reconstructed hydration microenvironment accelerates proton-coupled hydrogenation across chemically distinct substrates, enabling selective conversion of furfural to furfuryl alcohol, quinoline to tetrahydroquinoline, and nitrate to ammonia. In-situ spectroscopy and theoretical analysis collectively reveal that anion coordination simultaneously restructures the local Cu coordination environment and interfacial water network, thereby lowering the kinetic barrier for proton-coupled electron transfer. These findings establish coordinating anions as active molecular components of catalytic interfaces and introduce anion-site coupling as a general strategy for programming interfacial hydration and proton-transfer pathways in electrocatalytic synthesis.

item.title: Active Site Migration in Heterogeneous Hydrogenation by Coupling N‐Doped Carbon and Platinum
item.description:
Coupling H2${\rm H}_2$ activation on Pt/C with substrate reduction on N-doped carbon redirects the hydrogenation flux toward the carbon phase, producing an apparent migration of the operative active site.


ABSTRACT

In heterogeneous hydrogenation, porous carbon supports are usually treated as passive dispersants or electronic scaffolds for metal nanoparticles. Here, we show that in specifically designed N-doped carbon electrically coupled to Pt, the operative reduction locus can shift between catalyst components. Using p-nitrophenol (pNP) hydrogenation as a model reaction, we decouple hydrogen activation from substrate reduction in unbiased electrochemical and thermochemical configurations. While Pt/C is required for hydrogen activation, the nitrogen-doped TCNQ900 carbon acts as an efficient pNP reduction interface once supplied with H2${\rm H}_2$-derived electrons and protons. Electrochemical measurements show that coupling to TCNQ900 displaces Pt/C from its H2${\rm H}_2$/H+${\rm H}^+$ equilibrium along its hydrogen oxidation polarization curve, establishing a mixed-potential-driven electron flux toward the carbon phase. Under high H2${\rm H}_2$-activation capacity, Pt-centered (thermochemical) and carbon-centered reductions (electrochemical) operate in parallel, increasing the overall rate. Under H2${\rm H}_2$-activation-limited conditions, electrical coupling relocates the dominant reduction locus from Pt/C to TCNQ900 with little change in total rate. We describe this reversible redistribution of catalytic function as active-site migration. These results show that carbons can be chemically designed to serve not as passive supports, but as electronically coupled reduction interfaces that redirect hydrogenation pathways in multicomponent catalysts.

item.title: Synergistic Coordination and Crosslinking Strategy for Scalable, Self‐Repairable C2H4/C2H6 Separation Membranes
item.description:
Highly compatible, high-loaded UTSA-280-integrated MMMs were synthesized via a synergistic coordination and crosslinking strategy. This membrane combines high interfacial compatibility, excellent economic efficiency, a robust and self-repairable framework, and promising scale-up potential. Its ability to sustain stable operation at 7 bar demonstrates considerable promise for practical applications.


ABSTRACT

Ethylene/ethane (C2H4/C2H6) separation is one of the most energy-intensive processes in the chemical industry, and membrane technology offers a promising low-energy alternative. However, conventional mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) suffer from poor filler dispersion and interfacial defects, especially at high MOF loadings. Here we report a synergistic coordination and crosslinking strategy to fabricate highly compatible, high-loaded UTSA-280-integrated hydrogel MMMs for efficient C2H4/C2H6 separation. By exploiting the dual role of calcium ions (Ca2+), which simultaneously coordinate with squaric acid to grow UTSA-280 and crosslink sodium alginate (SA) chains, we achieve in situ growth of uniformly dispersed UTSA-280 nanoparticles (mean size 4.32 nm) within a semisolid hydrogel network. The resulting membrane exhibits a high MOF loading of 27.39 wt%, a C2H4/C2H6 mixture separation factor of 4.0 at 7 bar, and stable operation for over 1780 h. The hydrogel matrix also confers a remarkable self-repair capability, fully restoring separation performance after mechanical damage. Moreover, a 200 cm2 large-area membrane was readily fabricated, demonstrating a cost-effective route to scalable ethylene purification.

item.title: Programmable Interfacial Evolution in Seawater Iodine Batteries Guided by an Electrochemical Vector‐Coupled Free‐Energy Descriptor
item.description:
An electrochemically programmed adaptive interface dynamically couples electric-field evolution with halogen coordination thermodynamics, creating a responsive chemical reservoir that regulates reactive iodine intermediates. This adaptive halogen regulation overcomes the stability-accessibility trade-off, enabling reversible high-valence iodine conversion and durable multi-electron seawater energy storage.


ABSTRACT

Interface, as predominant electrochemical reaction region at the metal anode, has to face challenging issues in harsh seawater environment. Highly reactive soluble halogen intermediates can facilitate the multiple electron transfer process during electrochemical reaction, but the severe shuttle behaviors and cascade corrosion would become more serious in chlorine enriched seawater electrolyte. Conventional solution focused on static interfacial regulation with strong confinement, the lack of dynamical electrochemical response results in irreversible active iodine loss, further accelerate the battery failure. Given that, we proposed a novel theoretical descriptor to qualify electrochemical vector coupled free energy landscape, denoted as 𝒢ev (E, ΔG 0). By coupling electric filed with free energy, the electrochemically programming interface with dynamic self-adaptive halogen regulation (AHR) can be described quantitively. Taking an α-aminoketone-contained bio-interface as an example, along with the polarization variation over electrochemical reaction, the interface enables reversible capture to release shift of halogen intermediates, and thus realize reversible modulation of Cl-coordinated iodine species by leveraging thermodynamic gating mechanism. An emergency power supply system based on seawater-activated flexible fiber batteries could well operate in underwater portable situation. Our work unveils a novel research perspective on interface regulation strategies, to build an initiative adaptive interface rather than conventional ways.

item.title: Spin and Charge Engineering of a BiCuMn Nanoalloy Catalyst for Industrial‐Scale Electrosynthesis of Glycine
item.description:
Spin and charge engineering of a BiCuMn nanoalloy catalyst enables industrial-scale glycine electrosynthesis from nitrate and glyoxylic acid. Bi–Cu accelerates nitrate-to-*NO conversion via d-p hybridization, while Mn-mediated spin regulation promotes neighboring Bi-*NO hydrogenation and subsequent C–N coupling, delivering high selectivity, productivity, and long-term stability.


ABSTRACT

Electrocatalytic C–N coupling provides a sustainable route for α-amino acids, yet its practicality is limited by poor selectivity and durability at industrially relevant current densities. Here, we report a Bi-based nanoalloy catalyst with atomically dispersed Cu and Mn (BiCuMn@C) for industrial-level glycine electrosynthesis. Experimental and theoretical results reveal that Cu modulates the electronic structure of Bi sites via d-p hybridization, enhancing the adsorption/activation of nitrogen-containing species, while spin-polarized electrons from Mn are delivered to adjacent *NO intermediates, promoting their hydrogenation to *NHO on the pathway to NH2OH. This spin-charge engineering disrupts the intrinsic scaling relationship between *NO and *NHO adsorption, enabling simultaneous enhancement of activity and selectivity. As a result, BiCuMn@C achieves a glycine Faradaic efficiency of 78.9% at a current density of 533.1 mA cm−2, corresponding to a yield rate of 1569 µmol h−1 cm−2, and extends to the efficient synthesis of five additional amino acids. In a membrane-electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer, the catalyst sustains stable operation for over 1000 h with a cumulative glycine production exceeding 1 mol. This work achieves one of the best overall performances reported to date and provides practical design guidance for the industrially relevant electrosynthesis of α-amino acids.

item.title: Intrinsic Catalyst Reactivity—not Matched Surfactant Polarity—Drives Yield Differences in Aqueous Cross‐Coupling
item.description:
An aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura reaction was probed by fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy and spatially resolved spectroscopy. Triethylamine-rich organic droplets, rather than surfactant micelles, were identified as the main microreactors, disproving a proposed product–surfactant polarity-matching inhibition mechanism. Catalyst reactivity instead emerged as the key parameter, enabling predictive identification of faster reaction conditions.


ABSTRACT

Micelles in aqueous–organic syntheses are commonly assumed to be the primary reaction sites that colocalize and transform reactants. However, under synthetically relevant high-concentration conditions, including those used at scale in industrial pharmaceutical synthesis, phase separation may alter this simplified picture in poorly understood ways. Here, we investigate an aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling producing a fluorescent product using triethylamine base and Kolliphor EL or Tween 80 surfactants. Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM), dual-channel imaging, and microspectroscopy reveal that micrometer-scale triethylamine-rich organic droplets, rather than nanoscale surfactant micelles, function as the predominant reaction sites. Direct measurements of droplet and micelle molecular compositions disprove a proposed product-saturation inhibition mechanism based on surfactant polarity matching. Instead, the observed yield differences arise primarily from intrinsic catalyst reactivity. Surfactant-free “on-water” reactions further show that micelles are not required for productive coupling, supporting a primary role for surfactant in homogenization and mass transfer rather than creation of selective reaction compartments. This revised mechanistic assignment redirected reaction optimization from surfactant polarity to catalyst reactivity, affording 95% conversion to product in 20 min versus 26% under prior conditions. These findings challenge prevailing assumptions regarding micellar catalysis and demonstrate how microscale imaging can enable predictive optimization of aqueous reactions.

item.title: Thorium and Uranium Cyaphido and Pnictaethynolato Complexes
item.description:
The synthesis of a homologous series of tris(hexamethyldisilyl)amide thorium(IV) and uranium(IV) complexes bearing phosphaethynolate (OCP–), arsaethynolate (OCAs–), and cyaphide (CP–) ligands is reported. Geometric differences in the structures adopted by these compounds suggest notable differences in the nature of the actinide–pseudohalogen interactions.


ABSTRACT

The synthesis of a homologous series of tris(hexamethyldisilazide) thorium(IV) and uranium(IV) complexes bearing phosphaethynolate (OCP), arsaethynolate (OCAs), and cyaphide (CP) ligands is reported. These species were characterized by multi-element NMR spectroscopy (1H, 13C{1H} and 31P), IR spectroscopy and single-crystal x-ray diffraction. A structural comparison of the compounds reveals interesting geometric variations, with the pnictaethynolate complexes favoring strictly trigonal pyramidal geometries, whereas the cyaphide compounds display moderately more tetrahedral coordination environments, approaching those of the chlorido precursors [An{N(SiMe3)2}3Cl] (An = U, Th). We attribute these subtle structural differences to the covalency of the metal–ligand interactions. This hypothesis was probed using density functional theory, which showed that the computed gas-phase structures of the compounds do indeed match those determined experimentally. Electronically speaking, the An–OCE bonds were found to be almost purely ionic (with polarization to the pseudo-halide oxygen atoms ranging from 95%–100%). In these complexes, the highly Lewis acidic character of the metals pulls them into the plane defined by the amide ligands to maximize metal–hexamethyldisilazide interactions. By contrast, the An–CP bonds have greater covalent character than those observed for the pnictaethynolate complexes, with a lesser degree of polarization and higher Wiberg bond indices.

item.title: Nickel‐Catalyzed Enantio‐ and Regioselective Addition of Silicon and Boron Nucleophiles to Methylene Cyclobutene for the Construction of Quaternary Stereocenters
item.description:
A nickel-catalyzed addition of silicon and boron nucleophiles to methylene cyclobutenes enables the facile synthesis of highly enantioenriched silicon- and boron-substituted cyclobutenes containing a stereogenic quaternary carbon atom with a silyl or boryl group as a synthetic linchpin. Enantiomeric excesses are very high throughout, and the regioselectivity is always in favor of the depicted regioisomer.


ABSTRACT

A nickel-catalyzed enantio- and regioselective addition of silicon and boron nucleophiles to the 1,3-diene unit of methylene cyclobutenes is reported. Si─B and B─B reagents serve as silicon and boron pronucleophiles, respectively. Notably, this protocol not only constitutes the unprecedented catalytic asymmetric synthesis of cyclobutanes containing a stereogenic, silicon-substituted quaternary carbon atom but also provides an efficient access to their boron-substituted analogs. The transformation proceeds with excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee) and regioisomeric ratios (up to r.r. > 20:1). The substrate scope is broad, and the resulting silicon- and boron-substituted products can be engaged in diverse downstream functional-group manipulations, underscoring the synthetic utility of this methodology.

item.title: Engineered Pore Bisection by a Cymbal‐Shaped Cycloaliphatic Pillar in a Zn‐Triazolate Metal–Organic Framework (MOF) for Selective CO2 Capture
item.description:
A mechanochemically synthesized Zn-triazolate metal–organic framework (MOF) incorporating the cymbal-shape bicyclopentane-core as a pillar bisects the pore space into ultramicropore sub-pockets, that selectively confine CO2. Framework flexibility, robust yet regenerable CO2 binding and humidity-tolerant breakthrough performance are preserved in a processable polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) composite.


ABSTRACT

Physisorbents combining ultramicroporosity, high CO2 affinity, and humidity tolerance remain a challenge in carbon-capture materials. MOFs based on flexible Zn-triazolate layers have emerged as a promising platform; however, balancing pore size, confinement, and regeneration remains nontrivial. Here we introduce a new pillared-layer MOF, ZnTzBCP, constructed from Zn2 + cations, 1,2,4-triazolate (Tz) linkers, and the 3-dimensional cycloaliphatic bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane-1,3-dicarboxylate (BCP) linker. Liquid-assisted mechanochemical grinding affords a crystalline material in which the rigid BCP pillars with a cymbal-shaped core bisect the pore space into symmetric twin ultramicropores with dimensions commensurate with the CO2 kinetic diameter. Combined PXRD/PW-DFT/Rietveld analysis integrated with gas sorption, calorimetry, and CO2-loaded structural refinement reveals reversible, guest-responsive flexibility of the Zn-Tz layers through anisotropic swelling of the MOF with CO2 molecules generating multiple cooperative C─H···O interactions with both ligands and yielding high adsorption enthalpies of 41 kJ/mol. These properties are retained in a PVDF composite, which demonstrates stable, cyclic CO2 capture under humid breakthrough conditions with minimal thermal regeneration (333 K) and outstanding selectivity for CO2 over nitrogen of 226. These findings position the linkers with a cymbal-shaped core as powerful pore-controlling elements for the design of ultramicroporous MOFs capable of selective CO2 capture under operative conditions.

item.title: Single Chiroptical Pulse in Non‐Equilibrium Supramolecular Systems via Inter‐Macrocyclic Crosstalk
item.description:
Guest-mediated “communication” between two non-interacting macrocycles—pillar[5]arene (P8) and prism[5]arene (N4)—yields a tunable non-reactive aperiodic transient fluctuation. This transient fluctuation originates from multiple dynamic couplings in competitive binding equilibrium and the flat-plane inversion-induced reversal (FIIPC) effect, offering a novel strategy for programming time-dependent chiroptical responses.


ABSTRACT

Can an autonomous triphasic temporal pulse emerge in supramolecular architectures without relying on chemical transformations or external chemical fuel? Here, we demonstrate sequential chiroptical sign reversals in a time-dependent, aperiodic circular dichroism waveform excursion governed purely by non-covalent binding kinetics in a dual-receptor network of pillar[5]arene and prism[5]arene. Challenging an established chiral equilibrium with an antipodal alanine derivative induces an out-of-equilibrium optical pulse that inverts the chiroptical sign before settling into a persistent state. This transient behavior originates from the synergy between mismatched macrocyclic binding/unbinding rates and ultra-fast racemization of planar chirality during competitive ligand exchange, as verified by time-resolved spectroscopy and kinetic modeling. Tailoring receptor substituents and component ratios enables straightforward regulation over both duration and amplitude of the transient response. By establishing indirect intermolecular signal relays through shared effectors, this work provides a transformative blueprint for engineering dissipative systems-level dynamics in non-reactive, life-like materials.

item.title: Enantioselective Coupling of 1,3‐Dienes and Vinyl Acetate for the Synthesis of Succinic Acids and β‐ and γ‐Amino Acids
item.description:
Readily accessible 1,3-dienes and vinyl carboxylates undergo highly regio- and enantioselective [(L*) Co(I)]+-catalyzed heterodimerization reactions giving 1,4-skipped dienes. The electronically different double bonds flanking the newly created stereogenic center are amenable to chemoselective transformations into products that can serve as precursors for several medicinally important classes of compounds.


ABSTRACT

Catalyzed by cationic cobalt(I) complexes, [(L*)Co]+ [X]−, 1,3-dienes and vinyl carboxylates, two readily accessible electron-rich class of substrates, undergo highly regio- and enantioselective heterodimerization giving skipped 1,4-dienes with two configurationally defined, electronically differentiated double bonds flanking the newly formed stereogenic center (er typically >96:4). Among the numerous chelating bis-phosphine and phosphino-oxazoline ligands, commercially available P-centered chiral ligand, (2S, 2’S, 3S, 3’S)-MeO-BIBOP incorporating a dibenzooxaphophole scaffold was found to be uniquely suited to give high yields and excellent regio- and enantioselectivities. Notably, in these additions, vinyl acetate serves as an acetaldehyde enolate surrogate. Configurations of the double bonds and of the stereogenic center were established by the crystal structure of the adduct from vinyl ester of (S)-naproxen and (E)-1,3-nonadiene. The reaction has wide scope in both the 1,3-dienes and a surprisingly broad array of highly functionalized vinyl esters, including vinyl sorbate, vinyl α-chloroacetate, vinyl methacrylate, vinyl α-phenyl acrylate, and vinyl esters of α-amino acids. Functional groups, such as bromide, aldehyde, and vinyl groups, are tolerated in the vinyl esters. The coupling products carry multiple latent functionalities enabling their facile conversions to several useful classes of compounds, among them, chiral succinic acids, β- and γ-amino acids, and 4-alkyl γ-butyrolactams.

item.title: Aqueous π‐Hole Interactions Enabled by Chiral Perfluoroarene Amphiphiles
item.description:
A series of chiral perfluoroarene amphiphiles based on an octafluoronaphthalene scaffold, in which the amphiphilicity, self-assembly behavior, and confined microenvironment were regulated through end-group engineering, enabling selective recognition and photophysical modulation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), providing a new design strategy for aqueous supramolecular recognition, aromatic guest aggregation regulation, and the construction of chiral photofunctional materials based on π-hole-based interactions.


ABSTRACT

Arene-perfluoroarene (AP) interactions, as a representative class of π-hole-driven noncovalent interactions, have demonstrated unique advantages in molecular recognition and supramolecular assembly. However, the precise regulation of hydrophobic aromatic molecules in aqueous environments through AP interactions remains challenging. Herein, we designed and constructed a series of chiral perfluoroarene amphiphiles based on an octafluoronaphthalene scaffold, in which the amphiphilicity, self-assembly behavior, and confined microenvironment were regulated through end-group engineering, enabling selective recognition and photophysical modulation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). These perfluoroarene amphiphiles readily formed stable lamellar vesicular assemblies in aqueous solution. The π-hole region of the perfluoroarene moiety interacted with PAHs through AP interactions, facilitating the incorporation of guest molecules into the confined lamellar domains. Consequently, a variety of hydrophobic PAHs were successfully encapsulated in aqueous media, accompanied by effective modulation of their excited-state behaviors. Moreover, the chiral confined microenvironment induced chiroptical responses from achiral PAHs, enabling efficient chirality transfer. This work provides a new design strategy for aqueous supramolecular recognition, aromatic guest aggregation regulation, and the construction of chiral photofunctional materials based on AP interactions.

item.title: Electric‐Field‐Manipulated Reaction Pathway Engineering in Lupinus micranthus‐Like High‐Entropy Alloy Nanowires for Direct Alcohol Fuel Cells
item.description:
The Lupinus micranthus-like PtFeCoIrRhCu high-entropy alloy nanowires generate strain-charge-mediated local electric field that enables a capture-migration-dissociation relay and interfacial water ordering for low-potential *OH generation. The generated *OH species steer methanol oxidation toward the non-CO pathway (*CHO → *CH(OH)2) and accelerate *CO oxidative removal, resulting in high catalytic activity and durable fuel cell performances.


ABSTRACT

Electrocatalytic alcohol oxidation in direct fuel cells is constrained by CO poisoning and insufficient hydroxyl generation at low potentials. Here we show that anisotropic PtFeCoIrRhCu high-entropy alloy nanowires with Lupinus micranthus-like morphology generate a local electric field through coupling of strain-induced lattice distortion with charge redistribution, enabling a directional capture-migration-dissociation relay of interfacial water for efficient low-potential hydroxyl generation, in which H2O is preferentially captured at Fe/Co sites, migrates under field polarization, and dissociates at Rh/Ir sites. In situ infrared spectroscopy reveals that the electric field reorganizes interfacial water into a more ordered hydrogen-bond network, facilitating water activation. Density functional theory calculations, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry and operando electrochemical impedance spectroscopy further demonstrate that the generated hydroxyl species accelerate CO oxidative removal and promote the non-CO oxidation pathway. Consequently, the catalyst achieves a methanol oxidation mass activity of 3.76 A mgPt −1, 8.36 times that of Pt/C, together with a direct methanol fuel cell peak power density of 163.06 mW cm−2 and stable membrane-electrode operation for 200 h at 100 mA cm−2. These findings establish strain–charge coupling as a general strategy for engineering interfacial water activation and directing reaction-pathway selectivity in multimetallic electrocatalysts.

item.title: Manganese‐Catalyzed Electrochemical Nitrogenative‐Oxygenative Cleavage of Alkenes
item.description:
Manganese electrocatalysis enables chemoselective nitrogenative-oxygenative alkene cleavage to ketonitriles, while kinetic and spectroscopic studies elucidate its modus operandi by revealing precatalyst activation involving a mixed-valent oxo-bridged dimanganese species.


ABSTRACT

Herein, we report a manganese-catalyzed electrochemical nitrogenative-oxygenative scission of olefins to nitriles and carbonyls. Mechanistic and kinetic studies reveal distinct precatalyst-activation and productive-turnover regimes, and support conversion of the manganese precursor into a mixed-valent oxo-bridged dimanganese(III/IV) species, followed by azide-dependent formation of a product-forming manganese species. Notably, polyunsaturated substrates can undergo alkene-chemoselective cleavage with preferential reaction at the more substituted C═C bond, while the present protocol enables unprecedented reactivity towards activated and unactivated alkenes with broad functional-group tolerance.

item.title: Metal–Backboned Architectures Enable Magneto–Spin–Charge Engineering for High–Performance Li–CO2 Batteries
item.description:
We propose a cobalt-backboned oligomer material for Li–CO2 batteries that enables effective spin manipulation. Magnetic field drives charge redistribution and spin polarization, shifting Co from low-spin to high-spin state, enhancing CO2 adsorption. The resulting battery achieves a low overpotential of 1.06 V and stable operation over 2700 h. This metal-backboned architecture offers a new spin-based strategy to boost Li–CO2 battery kinetics.


ABSTRACT

Simultaneous CO2 conversion and high–energy–density energy storage are urgently needed for sustainable energy systems where Li–CO2 batteries provide an ideal solution, yet their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish CO2 redox kinetics. Emerging metal–backboned molecules, which contain numerous metal atoms as catalytically active sites, are expected to accelerate CO2 reduction reaction kinetics due to their unique architectures and properties. Herein, we report a novel mixed–valence cobalt–backboned polymer with effective spin manipulation as an efficient electrocatalyst and conductive scaffold for Li–CO2 batteries, which enables a low overpotential of 1.06 V and outstanding stable cycling over 2700 h. An external magnetic field drives Co centers from low–spin to high–spin configuration and enhances intermetallic intervalence charge transfer, synergistically strengthening CO2 adsorption and activation by increasing unpaired electron orbital occupancy and facilitating electron transfer to CO2 antibonding orbitals. This work establishes metal–backboned architectures as a versatile platform for spin–charge cooperative engineering, opening a new avenue for kinetically accelerated next–generation energy storage systems.

item.title: Solvation‐Directed Electric Double Layer Formation in Low‐Concentration Electrolytes
item.description:
Solvation asymmetry directs electric double layer (EDL) formation in low-concentration electrolytes. Large, weakly coordinating anions accumulate at the interface to form a persistent charge-shielding layer, while small, strongly coordinating anions are dynamically driven deeper into the Helmholtz region under polarization and modulate interfacial (de)solvation kinetics. This cooperative mechanism creates a self-adaptive EDL that couples electrostatic stabilization with interfacial chemistry.


ABSTRACT

The electric double layer (EDL) governs interfacial stability in lithium metal batteries, yet its rational design remains constrained by concentrated electrolytes or complex solvent systems. Here we demonstrate that the EDL in low-concentration electrolytes (LCEs) can be rationally programmed through anion selection based on their solvation behavior, decoupling interfacial stability from the heavy consumption of lithium salts and sophisticated solvent blends. By systematically screening anions with distinct Li+-anion coordination strengths and steric profiles, we formulate a mixed-anion LCE and uncover a fundamental principle: large, weakly coordinatinganions (WCAs) accumulate at the interface to form a persistent charge-shielding layer, whereas small, strongly coordinating anions (SCAs) are dynamically driven deeper into the Helmholtz region under polarization, where they actively modulate interfacial (de)solvation kinetics. This solvation-defined division of labor creates a rationally designed, self-adaptive EDL that couples electrostatic stabilization with interfacial chemistry. Beyond offering a high-performance LCE formulation, this work establishes a direct and mechanistic linkage between bulk solvation architecture and interfacial EDL organization in dilute electrolytes, revealing that the EDL can itself be programmed through anion-specific solvation motifs to dictate interfacial stability, introducing a design paradigm for materially efficient electrolyte engineering based on solvation-directed EDL formation.

item.title: The Self‐Powered Nanofiltration Membrane Driven by Pulsed Pressure for Efficient Selective Separation of Na+/Ca2+
item.description:
Pulsed pressure activates the direct piezoelectric response of a piezoelectric nanofiltration membrane (PQNF) and generates a transient electric field. This transient electric field coupled with the positively charged selective layer that enhances electrostatic repulsion and enables efficient Na+/Ca2+ separation with high Ca2+ rejection and long-term stability.


ABSTRACT

Enhancing electrostatic repulsion against divalent cations in the selective layer is effective in improving monovalent/divalent cation separation in nanofiltration. However, conventional grafting and coating strategies are limited by insufficient reaction sites or poor coating stability, both of which restrict further improvements in monovalent/divalent cation selectivity. Herein, a positively charged nanofiltration membrane with a piezoelectric response (PQNF) was designed via reverse thermally induced phase separation (RTIPS) coupled with interfacial polymerization (IP). RTIPS endowed the poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) substrate with a sponge-like pore structure, a narrow pore-size distribution, and a high β-phase content. Subsequently, the PQNF membrane was prepared via IP, quaternization, and corona poling. Under pulsed pressure operation, a periodic in situ voltage of 0.4 V was generated, which contributed to the 98.7% Ca2+ rejection and a Na+/Ca2+ separation factor of 89.6. The membrane also maintained stable separation performance over 144 h and showed enhanced antifouling performance under pulsed pressure operation in a 14 h fouling test. Finally, an “electrostatic–piezoelectric synergistic enhancement” separation mechanism was proposed and supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

item.title: Mechanism of Alkene Skeletal Isomerization in Zeolites Revealed by Coupled‐Cluster Accurate Free‐Energy Simulations
item.description:
Are carbocations persistent intermediates in zeolite catalysis? Machine-learning potentials incorporating local coupled-cluster corrections enable free-energy simulations of n-butene isomerization in chabazite. The resulting landscape reveals transient ionic configurations and challenges the assignment of protonated methylcyclopropane (PMCP) as a metastable intermediate, offering a practical route to uncover reaction mechanisms beyond conventional DFT.


ABSTRACT

The mechanism of Brønsted acid-catalyzed transformations in zeolites is generally described in terms of carbocationic intermediates, yet their thermodynamic stability and mechanistic role remain controversial. Resolving this issue requires chemically accurate free-energy simulations, which are beyond the reach of conventional density functional theory (DFT) and prohibitively expensive at the coupled-cluster level. Here, we combine a cluster-based QM/QM Δ$\Delta$-learning strategy with a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to enable molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with near-CCSD(T) accuracy. Applied to the skeletal isomerization of n-butene in chabazite, the resulting free-energy surfaces (FESs) reveal a mechanistic picture that differs qualitatively from that predicted by generalized-gradient approximation (GGA) functionals. Rather than proceeding through persistent carbocationic intermediates, the reaction is governed by a cascade of highly transient ionic configurations, while protonated methylcyclopropane (PMCP) is identified as a short-lived reactive configuration rather than a genuine metastable intermediate. These findings provide a more physically consistent description of one of the prototypical reactions in zeolite catalysis. More generally, the methodology introduced here provides a practical route toward chemically accurate free-energy simulations of heterogeneous catalytic reactions involving highly reactive charged species, opening the way to quantitative mechanistic studies of complex catalytic processes.

item.title: Heteroatom‐Modulated Aggregation of Diketopyrrolopyrrole Derivatives by Single‐Atom Substitution to Construct NIR‐II‐Absorbing Photothermal Agents With Over 90% Efficiency
item.description:
An atom-level strategy of heteroatom-modulated aggregation is proposed by introducing the distinct electronegativities of sulfur and oxygen to adjust the electrostatic potential distributions, thereby precisely tailoring intermolecular interactions to induce the transformation from H- to J-aggregation to construct a NIR-II-absorbing organic small-molecule nanoagent for synergistic photothermal immunotherapy.


ABSTRACT

Organic small-molecule photothermal materials with second near-infrared (NIR-II) absorption have attracted enormous interest for biomedical applications, yet simultaneously achieving strong NIR-II absorption and high photothermal conversion efficiency remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report to conduct the heteroatom-modulated aggregation of diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) derivatives (named as DAQ-T and DAQ-Fu) by single-atom substitution to construct high-performance NIR-II-absorbing photothermal agents. Single-crystal x-ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations reveal that oxygen-for-sulfur substitution precisely modulates electrostatic potential distributions and tailors intermolecular π–π interactions by leveraging the distinct electronegativities of chalcogens, driving a transformation from H-aggregation in DAQ-T to J-aggregation in DAQ-Fu. The resulting J-aggregated DAQ-Fu nanoparticles feature a distinct absorption band at 1064 nm with a molar extinction coefficient of 3.26 × 104 L mol−1 cm−1, and exhibit an outstanding photothermal conversion efficiency of 92.4%. This photothermal effect exerts potent antitumor efficacy by regulating apoptosis and immune-related signaling pathways, enabling the synergy of photothermal therapy and as-induced immunogenic cell death to suppress both primary and distant tumors growth with about 90% and 63% inhibition rates, respectively, under biocompatible irradiation. This work demonstrates atom-precise aggregation modulation, offering a promising pathway to engineer NIR-II-absorbing organic small-molecule photothermal agents for synergistic photothermal cancer immunotherapy.

item.title: Fast‐Discharge‐Induced Non‐Equilibrium Phase Transition in Ni‐Rich Layered Oxide Cathode at High Voltage
item.description:
High time-resolved 2D XRD reveals the origin of structural degradation for Ni-rich NCM-83 cathodes under high-rate (≥4C). The separation of H2 and H3 phases at high voltage (4.5 V→4.0 V) during fast discharge (≥4C) produces pronounced lattice displacement and strain which lower the migration barrier for Ni, thereby accelerating irreversible rock-salt formation in the bulk and eventual structural collapse.


ABSTRACT

The rapid adoption of electric vehicles necessitates lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) that can sustain extreme fast charging (XFC) without rapid degradation. Ni-rich layered cathodes deliver high energy density, yet their poor stability under high-rate operation limits practical deployment and the mechanistic origin of fast capacity decay remains poorly understood. Here, using high time-resolved operando XRD, together with theoretical analyses, we reveal that a rate-dependent non-equilibrium H3→H2 phase transition under rapid discharge (≥4 C) induces huge lattice displacement and nanoscale strain, which significantly lower the migration barrier for Ni, thereby promoting irreversible rock-salt phase formation and structural collapse. Importantly, guided by this mechanistic understanding, we propose a cycling protocol introducing a brief low-rate discharge step at high voltage (4.5 V→4.0 V), which effectively suppresses the detrimental H2+H3 phase separation and generation of internal stress. Compared to that of the cell under constant high cycling rates (6 C), the capacity retention improves 29% for the one with optimized discharge procedure after 1000 cycles. These results clarify the underneath electrochemical–mechanical degradation behavior of Ni-rich layered cathodes at different rates (1/3 C, 1 C, 4 C, and 6 C), providing practical guidance for designing durable batteries with superior fast-charging abilities.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Enantioconvergent 1,4‐Difunctionalization of Homoallylic and Homopropargylic Alcohols via Radical‐Relay Deoxygenation
item.description:
A general and efficient platform for the enantioconvergent deoxygenative 1,4-difunctionalization of racemic homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols upon an unprecedented remote hydrogen atom transfer-triggered radical deoxygenation process is presented. Both 1,4-perfluoroalkylamidation and 1,4-cyanoperfluoroalkylation have been developed by copper/bisoxazoline asymmetric catalysis, enabling facile access to diverse chiral perfluoroalkyl-containing amides and nitriles with excellent enantiomeric excess.


ABSTRACT

Despite the long-recognized structural diversity and accessibility of homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols as synthetic building blocks, their deoxygenative radical difunctionalization remains a formidable challenge due to the lack of a linkage strategy integrating the respective functionalization of non-adjacent hydroxyl and alkene/alkyne groups. Herein, we present an efficient platform for the deoxygenative radical 1,4-difunctionalization of homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols through an unprecedented remote hydrogen atom transfer-triggered radical-relay deoxygenation process. Utilizing 1,3-benzodithiolylium as an effective hydroxyl-activating reagent, copper-catalyzed enantioconvergent 1,4-perfluoroalkylamidation and 1,4-cyanoperfluoroalkylation have been achieved with excellent regio- and enantioselectivity.

item.title: Quenching or Accelerating Large‐Scale Surface Reconstruction by the Lightest Element: Facet‐Dependent Hydrogen‐Induced Reconstruction (HIR)
item.description:
The facet-dependent kinetics of hydrogen-induced reconstruction (HIR) on Pd–Ag surfaces is revealed by machine-learning (ML)-based global potential-energy exploration combined with large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The outcomes underscore that hydrogen stabilizes Pd domains on Ag(111) but promotes Pd dispersion on Ag(100), thereby shaping Pd3 active motifs for selective acetylene hydrogenation.


ABSTRACT

Adsorbate-induced surface reconstruction is believed to be a critical determinant of catalyst performance under operando conditions. The Pd–Ag bimetallic catalyst, used industrially for selective acetylene hydrogenation, is thought to undergo hydrogen-induced surface reconstruction (HIR) that exposes Pd active sites. However, the kinetic origin of HIR remains unknown because hydrogen is difficult to image. Here, using large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we resolve the kinetics of H-driven reconstruction. On Pd-covered Ag surfaces, reconstruction initially involves Pd–Ag exchange at domain peripheries and Ag atoms popping up to encapsulate exposed Pd. This process is faster on (100) than on (111). Hydrogen suppresses reconstruction on (111) above 0.3 ML, but accelerates Pd dispersion and encapsulation on (100) mediated by transient Pd–H pair formation. This facet dependence arises from hydrogen-induced kinetic hindrance of edge Pd diffusion away from Pd domains on (111). Analysis of MD-derived surface structures further shows that the Pd3 triangular surface pattern favors selective acetylene hydrogenation, confirming HIR's role in determining active-site structure. These findings provide the first evidence for facet-dependent, large-scale surface reconstruction induced by the lightest element and establish HIR as a key determinant of catalytic activity and selectivity.

item.title: Thiophenol‐Catalyzed Anti‐Markovnikov Coupling of α‐Methylene‐γ‐Butenolides Under Visible Light: Total Synthesis of Aucklappalide A
item.description:
Visible-light thiophenol catalysis enables the first anti-Markovnikov intermolecular coupling of α-methylene-γ-butenolides under photocatalyst-free conditions. A sulfur-mediated photochemical manifold involving a competent thiophenol adduct promotes intermolecular C–C bond formation, providing concise access to complex disesquiterpenoid architectures, including aucklappalide A.


ABSTRACT

General methods for the selective anti-Markovnikov intermolecular coupling of electron-poor alkenes remain scarce. Herein, we report a visible-light-mediated, photocatalyst-free strategy for the anti-Markovnikov coupling of α-methylene-γ-butenolides using a simple formate/thiophenol reaction platform. The method enables the direct synthesis of structurally diverse homo- and cross-coupled disesquiterpenoid architectures from complex sesquiterpenoid lactones, including the first total synthesis of aucklappalide A. Mechanistic investigations support a distinct sulfur-mediated photochemical manifold involving a thiophenol adduct that provides access to the carbon-centered radical required for intermolecular C–C bond formation. These findings establish a photocatalyst-free approach to the redox-neutral anti-Markovnikov coupling of α-methylene-γ-butenolides, uncover a previously unrecognized sulfur-mediated radical manifold enabled by formate/thiophenol photochemistry, and suggest that related sulfur-centered radical processes may contribute to the biosynthesis of dimeric sesquiterpenoid lactones.

item.title: Catalytically Active Species and Sites in CO2 Hydrogenation Identified by Modulation Excitation Spectroscopy
item.description:
Rational design of better catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation requires detailed knowledge of the reaction mechanism including key intermediates and active sites. This Minireview discusses the potential of modulation excitation spectroscopy as a powerful tool to identify active species and sites as illustrated by the current literature, and gives an outlook on methodical extentions and applications beyond thermal catalysis.


ABSTRACT

Thermocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO2) hydrogenation has developed into an important sustainable route toward valuable fuels and chemicals, thereby reducing the greenhouse gas CO2 and supporting the energy transition. For a rational design of more efficient, selective, and stable catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation, detailed knowledge of the reaction mechanism, including key intermediates and active sites is required. Modulation excitation spectroscopy (MES) has emerged as a powerful tool to discriminate between catalytically active and (nonparticipating) spectator species and to identify active sites, and has been shown to provide important new mechanistic findings not accessible by steady-state approaches, contributing to the very intense debate on CO2 hydrogenation mechanisms. Despite its broad applicability, the MES method is still rarely used in catalysis research and has contributed to the mechanism of CO2 hydrogenation mainly by its combination with infrared spectroscopy. In this Minireview, the potential of MES for providing mechanistic insight on catalytic CO2 hydrogenation will be illustrated based on the current literature, followed by an outline of potential methodical extensions. Future prospects for the application of MES to mechanistic studies on CO2 activation beyond thermal catalysis, including photo- and electrocatalysis, as well as other areas of research will be discussed.

item.title: Guide DNAs Program Enzyme for Detection of Circulating Tumor DNA Without Target Denaturation and Amplification
item.description:
Chemically modified guide DNAs program λ exonuclease to access native double-stranded ctDNA at room temperature, enabling detection without target amplification or denaturation. Coupling this chemistry to a DNAzyme and single-molecule fluorescence readout supports sensitive EGFR L858R ctDNA analysis in plasma.


ABSTRACT

Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is fragmented, tumor-derived cell-free double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) whose low abundance and limited sequence accessibility complicate detection under mild conditions. Here we show that guide DNAs (gDNAs) can program an exonuclease to interrogate native dsDNA under mild conditions and convert this access into a single-molecule fluorescence readout. We found that gDNA 5′-terminal chemistry regulates λ exonuclease (λExo) recruitment. Among those termini, anionic 5′-phosphate and 5′-carboxyl-C10 phosphate enabled the strongest target-dependent processing. Molecular simulations suggested a possible structural basis for these activity differences based on terminal positioning within the catalytic pocket. Coupling the optimized 5′-carboxyl-C10 phosphate gDNA with 10–23 DNAzyme turnover generated a single-molecule fluorescence readout without target nucleic-acid amplification. The assay detected dsDNA down to 10 fM across 10–1000 fM, showed a statistically significant response at an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) L858R mutant fraction of 0.05% under the tested conditions, and was applied to 24 plasma samples (12 from patients with non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and 12 from healthy donors), achieving 91.7% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 95.8% accuracy, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.97. This work establishes gDNA-programmed enzyme access as a route for detecting low-abundance duplex tumor DNA.

item.title: Confinement Enables Direct Electrosynthesis of Acetaldoxime From CO and Nitrate
item.description:
We report a confinement-enhanced electrocatalytic route for acetaldoxime synthesis from CO and NO3 − via C–N coupling. By encapsulating ultrasmall Cu nanoparticles into SBA-15, the sluggish C–C dimerization is kinetically matched with rapid NO3 − reduction, favoring the oximation pathway and achieving a production rate of 255.1 mmol gcat. − 1 h− 1 with an 8.2% Faradaic efficiency, enabling sustainable co-upcycling of carbon and nitrogen wastes.


ABSTRACT

Aldoximes are vital feedstocks in the fields of medicine, agriculture, and industry, yet their conventional synthesis suffers from high environmental costs and carbon footprints. Here, we report a direct electrocatalytic route to acetaldoxime via CO and NO3 − co-reduction. The C–N coupling efficiency in this process hinges on the kinetic match between CO reduction and NO3 − reduction. Acetaldoxime synthesis exemplifies this challenge: sluggish C–C dimerization contrasts with rapid NO3 −RR, leading to over-reduction of nitrogen species to NH3. We hypothesized that a confinement strategy could selectively promote C–C dimerization and enrich acetaldehyde intermediate, thereby facilitating oximation. Ultrasmall Cu nanoparticles were encapsulated within SBA-15 mesopores to selectively accelerate the dimerization step. Combined operando Raman and in situ differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal that the confined Cu lowers the overpotential for the key C2 intermediate to align with that for NH2OH generation, enabling efficient C–N coupling to acetaldoxime. The optimized Cu@SBA-15 catalyst achieves an acetaldoxime production rate of 255.1 mmol gcat. − 1 h− 1 (partial current density: 24.6 mA cm− 2). This work establishes a sustainable pathway toward aldoximes, aligning with green chemistry principles while expanding the toolbox for electrocatalytic C–N bond formation.

item.title: An Acyclic Two‐Coordinate Stannyliumylidene Enables SnII/SnIV Redox Catalysis
item.description:
Less coordination, greater reactivity: An isolable, acyclic two-coordinate stannyliumylidene combines pronounced Lewis acidity with an accessible lone pair, enabling ambiphilic small-molecule activation. Its unusual electronic and structural flexibility unlocks Sn(II)/Sn(IV) redox catalysis in ketone hydrosilylation, supported by the isolation of a catalytically competent stannyliumylidene–ketone adduct and detailed mechanistic investigations.


ABSTRACT

Main-group redox catalysis hinges on a fundamental trade-off, that is, reactive p-block centres must be stable enough to isolate, yet flexible enough to cycle through oxidation states. In this regard, two-coordinate stannyliumylidene ions with an accessible lone pair and vacant p-orbital offer an attractive ambiphilic platform for engaging in redox processes. To date, most reported examples remain confined to π- or heteroatom-donor-stabilized rigid frameworks, and the isolation of a genuinely two-coordinate acyclic stannyliumylidene has remained elusive. Herein, we report the synthesis and isolation of a two-coordinate, acyclic, mono-N-heterocyclic-carbene-stabilized stannyliumylidene paired with a weakly coordinating [B(3,5-(CF3)2C6H3)4]− anion. Stripped of additional donor stabilization, the tin centre is rendered highly electrophilic while maintaining an accessible lone pair. This enhanced electrophilicity enabled capture of a stannyliumylidene–ketone adduct, the first structurally characterized ketone-bound tetryliumylidene intermediate that is directly implicated in a catalytic cycle. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, combining experimental results with theoretical calculations, reveal an Sn(II)/Sn(IV) redox manifold that drives catalytic turnover. Together, these results significantly expand the landscape of tin-based redox catalysis and highlight that accessing stable low-valent stannyliumylidene ions with a minimal coordination number and weaker donor stabilization is a feasible approach for unlocking transition-metal-like redox behaviour at the tin centre.

item.title: Radical Buffering by Isolated Ru and Fe Sites in ZSM‐5 for Selective Methane Oxidation to Formic Acid
item.description:
In ZSM-5 micropores, two independent single-atom populations cooperate without any metal–metal bond. Fe activates methane to methyl radicals while Ru activates H2O2 and buffers hydroxyl radicals. This radical buffering directs Eley-Rideal coupling toward formic acid, raising oxygenate productivity 2.2-fold over Fe/ZSM-5 under mild conditions.


ABSTRACT

The selective conversion of methane under mild conditions is limited by the uncontrolled reactivity of radical intermediates (·CH3, ·OH) generated during Fe-catalyzed oxidation with H2O2. Here we report a radical buffering strategy in which atomically dispersed Ru is co-loaded with Fe in ZSM-5 as an ·OH reservoir, steering intermediates toward selective Eley-Rideal-type coupling in the micropores. The Ru-Fe/ZSM-5 catalyst achieves an oxygenate productivity of 37.5 mmol·gcat −1·h−1 at 70°C with 95.7% oxygenate selectivity and 92.3% formic acid selectivity among liquid products, a 2.2-fold improvement over Fe/ZSM-5. Extended X-ray absorption fine structure analysis shows that Ru and Fe exist as two independent populations of single atoms with no metal–metal bonding. Electron paramagnetic resonance and in situ infrared spectroscopy show that Fe activates CH4 to ·CH3 while Ru activates H2O2 and holds part of the resulting ·OH. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that Ru binds ·OH more strongly than Fe (−3.130 compared to −2.738 eV), and dissociates H2O2 nearly thermoneutrally (+0.077 eV). Therefore ·OH is held on Ru rather than on the Fe. This work establishes radical buffering by independent single-atom populations in confined micropores as a design principle for controlling selectivity in radical-mediated catalysis.

item.title: Alternating Terpolymerization of CO2 With Cyclosilanes and Epoxides to A‐B‐C‐Sequenced Recyclable Poly(silyl ether–ester)
item.description:
Catalyzed alternating terpolymerization of CO2, cyclosilanes, and epoxides, driven by thermodynamically favorable silyl ether bond formation, produces A-B-C sequence-defined poly(silyl ether–ester)s with tunable structures and thermal properties as well as chemical recyclability and hydrolytic degradability under acidic or basic conditions.


ABSTRACT

Carbon dioxide (CO2)-derived polyesters represent an attractive yet underdeveloped class of sustainable polymers, with most existing CO2-based polyesters relying on carbonate linkages in their backbones with statistical or block sequences. Here, we introduce terpolymerization of CO2 with cyclosilanes and epoxides to access poly(silyl ether–ester) with perfectly alternating A-B-C (CO2-alt-cyclosilane-alt-epoxide) sequences. This terpolymerization is enabled by the thermodynamically favored formation of Si─O bonds, providing a driving force for efficient incorporation of both silalactones and epoxides into the terpolymer backbone in an alternating fashion. A range of epoxide and silacyclobutane substrates can be incorporated into the polyester, affording structurally diverse terpolymers. Notably, these polymers are stable thermally (T d up to 313°C) and hydrolytically (in neutral water) but can slowly degrade under acidic or basic conditions and be chemically depolymerized under mild catalytic conditions to recover the silalactone monomer.

item.title: Standardization Transformation of Softwood Protolignin to Benzoxazole Molecule With Tumor‐Selective Cytotoxicity
item.description:
The standardization transformation of softwood protolignin into the bioactive benzoxazole molecule C3-GLB-pCBA with tumor-selective cytotoxicity was first established.


ABSTRACT

The protolignin standardization transformation into high-value-added pharmaceutical chemicals requires elaborate strategy design and catalytic system construction. Herein, a novel lignin valorization pattern to produce G-lignin-derived benzoxazoles from softwood is achieved, which involves the tandem CRF transformation of lignocellulose to C3-alkyl guaiacol (C3-G), stoichiometric diazotization-reductive ammonification of C3-G to aminophenol C3-GAP, and photocatalytic cyclization of C3-GAP to the benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA. The whole process can yield 6.2 wt% benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA from the aromatic guaiacyl rings of the original softwood lignin. Furthermore, the in vitro cytotoxicity assays with human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells, normal human osteoblast cells (hFOB1.19), and mouse 3T3 fibroblasts confirm the potential tumor-selective cytotoxicity of the as-synthesized G-lignin-derived benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA. Further TEA and LCA indicate the sustainability of the synthesis process of C3-GLB-pCBA from softwood. The success of the tandem pattern may inspire further studies on the high-value utilization of lignin to produce pharmaceutical molecules.

item.title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
item.description:
A DETA-induced universal luminescence (DIUL) strategy converts non-conjugated, non-emissive small molecules into bright clusteroluminescent materials. Synergistic ionic (─BF4 −/─NH2 +) and hydrogen-bonding (─NH─/─NH2) dual forces drive through-space conjugation, yielding >70% quantum yields in water. The resulting probes enable high-contrast dual-color cellular, 3D tumor spheroid, and long-term zebrafish imaging, establishing a modular platform for non-traditional luminophores in bioimaging.


ABSTRACT

Non-traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π-conjugation are attractive for bio-applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non-luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)-induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non-conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster-based small molecules via synergistic dual-force: ionic (─BF4 −/─NH2 +) and hydrogen-bonding (─NH─/─NH2) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual-force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen-bond-dominated aggregation-induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high-contrast dual-color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long-term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non-covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

item.title: Advancing C3 Polymerization of Alkynylcyclopropanes via a Synergistic Lewis Acid/Brønsted Base/C(sp3)–H Bond System
item.description:
The high electronegativity and strong coordinating ability of C–C triple bonds often hinder their integration into donor-acceptor cyclopropane chemistry. Here, we establish a synergistic Lewis acid/Brønsted base/C(sp3)─H bond system that overcomes these intrinsic limitations, enabling controlled C3 polymerization of alkynylcyclopropanes (ACPs) and providing access to a series of advanced functional polymeric materials.


ABSTRACT

The integration of cyclopropane chemistry with polymer science could offer access to unique all-carbon polymers. However, the ring-opening polymerization (ROP) of cyclopropanes generally requires strong electron-donating and -withdrawing substituents, limiting the use of electronically less activated monomers such as 2-alkynylcyclopropane-1,1-dicarboxylates (ACPs). Here, we demonstrate that the synergistic combination of a Lewis acid and a Brønsted base overcomes the electronic limitations imposed by carbon–carbon triple bonds, including their high electronegativity and strong coordinating ability, enabling the unprecedented C3 ROP of ACPs. This process is regulated by a reversible-deactivation equilibrium mediated by chain-end C(sp3)─H bonds, affording well-defined polymers bearing alkyne side groups. The resulting functional polymers provide a versatile platform for applications ranging from stimulus-responsive sensing to Raman imaging.

item.title: [8+4]‐Connected Ether‐Oxygen‐Based 3D COF Redox Mediators for Durable Light‐Assisted Indirect Electrocatalysis
item.description:
A series of [8+4]-connected 3D COFs, TADM–TAPP–COF (M) (M = Ni, Mn, and Cu), has been constructed from ether-oxygen-based 8-connected ether-oxygen based building blocks and metalloporphyrin linkers that can serve as redox mediators for the highly durable light-assisted indirect electrocatalytic condensation cyclization reaction.


ABSTRACT

Ether-oxygen is a type of functional group with high chemical stability, electronic modulation capability, and imparted molecular flexibility, yet incorporating ether-oxygen groups into high-connectivity covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to explore their extended applications remains a challenge. Herein, we have designed a series of [8+4]-connected 3D COFs with scu topology, named TADM–TAPP–COF(M) (M = Ni, Mn, and Cu), by introducing eight-connected ether-oxygen based building blocks and metalloporphyrin nodes, which can be applied in high-stability light-assisted indirect electrocatalysis. These 3D COFs exhibit good crystallinity, nanosheet morphology, flexible 3D pore structure, abundant ether-oxygen groups and active metal sites, and excellent electrolyte affinity, which can act as efficient redox mediators. Impressively, the Ni-incorporated structure TADM–TAPP–COF (Ni) demonstrates high yield in the condensation cyclization reaction of aromatic aldehydes and 2-aminobenzenethiol to produce 2-phenylbenzothiazole (yields up to 96%), coupled with the simultaneous production of gas-phase H2 product (∼1.15 mmol g−1 h−1). Notably, it also shows remarkable stability (continuous reaction for 300 h), high recyclability (8 cycles), and scale-up production ability (about 2 g in a 12 h batch experiment) and wide substrate applicability, providing a valuable example for the structural design of catalysts toward light-assisted indirect electrocatalysis.

item.title: Heat‐Activated Reversible Conjugation Switching in Polymers Through Cooperative Ion Pairing
item.description:
A general cooperative ion-pair-regulated strategy for reversibly generating linear conjugation in polymers was developed to achieve reversible colorless-to-colored heat-activated behavior. Weakly coordinated alkali metal salts such as LiPF6 and NaPF6 promote lactone ring opening to generate thermally activated multicolor responses and rewritable invisible inks, while isopropanol coordination reversibly restores the nonconjugated colorless state.


ABSTRACT

Thermochromic conjugated polymers generally undergo transitions from colored to less-colored states upon heating due to disruption of π-conjugation. In contrast, heat-triggered switching from a colorless state to a more intensely colored conjugated state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a reversible conjugation-switching polymer system governed by cooperative interactions between metal cations and counteranions. By incorporating lactone-functionalized xanthene units directly into conjugated polymer backbones, weakly solvated Li+, Na+, and Ag+ ions, acting cooperatively with their weakly coordinating counteranions, induce lactone ring opening and establish linear conjugation along the polymer backbone, thereby producing pronounced optical responses. Coordination of the metal ions by isopropanol reverses the process and restores the colorless state. A series of conjugated copolymers displayed thermally activated multicolor responses spanning blue, green, yellow, orange, red, magenta, and black, enabling rewritable invisible-ink systems on paper substrates. Density functional theory calculations support a nearly barrierless Li+/PF6 − ion-pair-cooperation-promoted ring-opening process and reveal reversible switching between twisted nonconjugated and planar linearly conjugated states. These results establish a metal-ion-regulated conjugation-switching strategy for heat-activated colorless-to-colored switching and responsive optical materials.

item.title: Photoreduction of Chlorinated Volatile Waste Into C2+ Hydrocarbons
item.description:
We report here synthesis of the first nickel–sulfur anthraquinone complex and the first photoreduction system to convert a series of chlorinated volatile organic compounds into unsaturated C2+ hydrocarbons using visible light. The photocatalytic system is not only tolerant to the difficultly converted substrates with high chlorine content but also capable of generating multi-carbon products from the C1 compounds.


ABSTRACT

Chlorinated volatile organic compounds (Cl─VOCs) are a class of major environmental pollutants and potential human carcinogens. Dechlorination of Cl─VOC waste into harmless and value-added chemicals under mild conditions is highly desirable yet challenging, and cannot be achieved using current photocatalytic methods. Here, we report the synthesis of the first nickel anthraquinone–thiolate complex for photoreduction of a variety of Cl─VOCs into unsaturated C2+ hydrocarbons in good yields using visible light. Notably, the molecular system is capable of both reducing C2 Cl─VOCs with high chlorine content into acetylene and C─C coupling of C1 Cl─VOCs into ethylene and propylene. Mechanistic studies reveal that multielectron and multi-proton reduction of the nickel complex is critical in generating the catalytically active species for various reductive dechlorination transformations. This study provides a blueprint for the conversion of chlorinated waste into highly valuable chemicals using solar energy.

item.title: Single‐Atom Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption Enables Ultrafast Charge Transfer for Boosting Photocatalytic H2 Production
item.description:
Single-atom Ni (NiSA) cocatalysts spontaneously form a multi-hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalysis, creating a local electron-deficient environment. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration induces stronger d-p orbital hybridization across the NiSA–S interface, shortens the Ni–S bond, and builds a highly conductive charge-transfer channel for ultrafast electron extraction from CdS, thus driving efficient photocatalytic H2 evolution.


ABSTRACT

Single-atom cocatalysts with near-100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H2 evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono-hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified frameworks fail to capture the complexity of operando reaction environments, where the high coordination unsaturation of single atoms inevitably drives a transition toward multi-hydrogen adsorption states. Here, we demonstrate that an N-coordinated Ni single-atom cocatalyst (NiSA-N) forms a multi-hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalytic H2 evolution, significantly accelerating ultrafast charge transfer kinetics. Research results demonstrate that the adsorption of multiple hydrogen triggers spontaneous free-electron delocalization, rendering the Ni center into a unique electron-deficient (δ+) feature. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration enhances the interfacial d-p orbital hybridization between NiSA and S of CdS, effectively shortening the interfacial Ni–S bond to construct a highly conductive channel that facilitates ultrafast electron transfer from the CdS to NiSA cocatalyst, as elucidated by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Consequently, the NiSA-N/CdS system achieves an exceptional H2 evolution rate of 20.20 mmol h−1 g−1. This work identifies the multi-hydrogen adsorption state as a pivotal nexus linking surface chemistry to ultrafast dynamics, providing a conceptual framework for engineering high-performance catalysts for artificial photosynthesis.

item.title: Localized Dipoles Enable Synergistic Kinetic and Thermodynamic Piezoreforming of Waste Plastics
item.description:
This work presents a mechanically driven piezocatalytic reforming method for converting waste plastics into platform chemicals carbon monoxide (CO) under ambient conditions. Asymmetric Fe–Se–Mo channel induces local dipoles, kinetically suppressing carrier recombination and accelerating charge-proton transfer, while thermodynamically enhancing the adsorption of key intermediates and lowering the activation energy barrier. Therefore, we achieved a 30.5 times higher CO yield with stable long-term production compared to MoSe2 catalysts.


ABSTRACT

The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics.
